# FedRAMP NTC-0014 / CISA BOD 26-04 — mandatory VDR + VER adoption by 2026-12-07

## 1. Constraint

Two coupled federal actions in June 2026 convert UIAO's previously
open-ended vulnerability-reporting modernization gate into a **dated
obligation** and introduce one rule UIAO does not yet model:

1. **CISA Binding Operational Directive 26-04 — "Prioritizing Security
   Updates Based on Risk" (issued 2026-06-10).** BOD 26-04 **supersedes
   BOD 22-01 (KEV remediation) and BOD 19-02 (internet-accessible
   systems)** and replaces flat, severity-only patch deadlines with a
   **four-variable risk matrix**: (a) whether the asset is publicly
   exposed, (b) whether the vulnerability is in the CISA Known Exploited
   Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, (c) whether the exploit is
   automatable, and (d) the post-exploit technical impact. The four
   variables map to a remediation-timeline ladder ranging from **3
   calendar days plus mandatory forensic triage** (KEV + total system
   control) down to **"fix on next system upgrade."** A vulnerability may
   be **mitigated** until it is no longer automatable or
   internet-reachable in lieu of full remediation.

2. **FedRAMP Notice NTC-0014 — "FedRAMP Response to CISA BOD 26-04"
   (published 2026-06-16).** NTC-0014 announces that FedRAMP will
   **mandate adoption of the Vulnerability Detection and Response (VDR)
   and the new Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting (VER) rules by
   2026-12-07** to align FedRAMP Authorized cloud service offerings with
   BOD 26-04. VDR and VER are being **finalized inside the Consolidated
   Rules for 2026 (CR26)** by the end of June 2026. A notable new VER
   requirement is **VER-EVA-EIR (Evaluate Internet-Reachability)** — an
   evaluation determining whether a vulnerability is likely reachable
   over the internet (the trigger for the BOD 26-04 mitigate-until-not-
   reachable escape hatch).

The constraint UIAO names is the **gap between a now-dated FedRAMP
mandate and the substrate's current modelling**. UIAO pre-wired VDR as
the Pathway-1 "modernized" path in [ADR-043](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-043-fedramp-rfc-0026-ca7-integration.md)
/ [UIAO_132](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/fedramp-rfc-0026-ca7-integration.md),
but (i) the Pathway-1 migration trigger was written as the open-ended
"publication of the VDR Balance Improvement Release" with **no date**,
(ii) **VER is not modelled at all**, and (iii) the substrate's
self-imposed **flat 72-hour critical SLA** (ADR-043 D2) does not encode
BOD 26-04's four-variable tiered ladder.

> **Disambiguation.** `fedramp.gov/notices/0014/` is **Notice NTC-0014**,
> not **RFC-0014** (Phase Two Key Security Indicators). RFC-0014 is
> already integrated via ADR-047 / UIAO_133 / UIAO_137; the two share
> only the digit string `0014`. This finding concerns the Notice.

## 2. Evidence

### Primary sources

- **[FedRAMP NTC-0014 — Response to CISA BOD 26-04](https://www.fedramp.gov/notices/0014/)** —
  Published 2026-06-16. Announces mandatory VDR + VER adoption by
  2026-12-07; VDR/VER finalized within CR26 by end of June 2026.
- **[CISA BOD 26-04 — Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk](https://cyber.dhs.gov/bod/26-04/)** —
  Issued 2026-06-10. Four-variable risk matrix; remediation-timeline
  ladder (3-day + forensic triage → next upgrade); supersedes BOD 22-01
  and BOD 19-02; three-phase agency rollout (immediate / 60-day /
  180-day).
- **[FedRAMP Vulnerability Detection and Response (VDR) documentation](https://www.fedramp.gov/docs/vulnerability-detection-and-response/)** —
  VDR process: systematically identify, analyze, prioritize, mitigate,
  and remediate vulnerabilities within a cloud service offering.
- **[FedRAMP 20x — Vulnerability Detection and Response](https://www.fedramp.gov/docs/20x/vulnerability-detection-and-response/)** —
  20x-context VDR rule surface; VER-EVA-EIR internet-reachability
  evaluation.
- **[FedRAMP Changelog](https://www.fedramp.gov/changelog/)** —
  Authoritative publication timeline for the CR26 / VDR / VER releases.

### Provenance note

Dates and timeline tiers cited here (the 2026-12-07 mandate, the
BOD 26-04 3-day floor, the CR26 end-of-June finalization) are snapshot
facts as of the 2026-06-18 access date and must be re-verified against
the FedRAMP.gov and cyber.dhs.gov primary sources at any time this
finding is acted on, since CR26 is in active finalization. The
`fedramp.gov` and `cyber.dhs.gov` hosts geo-gate cloud CI runners
(see `.lycheeignore`); the URLs are human-navigable references.

## 3. Capability gap

Tied to specific UIAO_NNN capability statements:

1. **UIAO_132 §2.4 Pathway-1 migration gate is now time-bound, not
   open-ended.** The spec says UIAO flips affected adapters from
   `pathway-2-traditional` to `pathway-1-modernized` on "publication of
   the VDR Balance Improvement Release." NTC-0014 supplies the missing
   date (**2026-12-07**) and a regulatory hook (BOD 26-04). The
   substrate can no longer treat the migration as discretionary timing;
   the gate has effectively fired.

2. **VER is unmodelled (UIAO_132).** UIAO_132 models only VDR
   (RV5-CA07-VLN) and Collaborative ConMon (RV5-CA07-CCM). The new VER
   rule — and especially **VER-EVA-EIR (Evaluate Internet-Reachability)**
   — has no canon home, no adapter binding, and no evidence-emission
   row in [UIAO_133 §2.2](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/fedramp-20x-integration.md).

3. **The flat 72-hour critical SLA does not encode BOD 26-04's tiered
   ladder (ADR-043 D2 / UIAO_132 §2.2).** UIAO's self-imposed SLA is a
   single 72-hour critical-finding clock layered over a monthly cadence.
   BOD 26-04 keys remediation off four variables (exposure / KEV /
   automatability / impact). The substrate cannot yet *express* a
   per-finding SLA derived from that matrix.

4. **CR26 snapshot pin predates VDR/VER (ADR-061 / UIAO_137).** The
   vendored CR26 catalog is pinned at snapshot `c31eb04…`
   (`metadata.version 0.1.0`, a shell). VDR/VER finalize inside CR26 by
   end of June 2026, so a **snapshot-pin advance** (ADR-061 D2) is
   required to ingest them — and [UIAO_137](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/fedramp-cr26-ksi-mapping.md)
   explicitly **defers the CR26 FRR-group mapping**, which is where the
   VDR/VER requirements live. That deferred mapping is now on the
   critical path.

5. **KSI themes VDR/VER lean on have zero local-rule coverage.** Per
   UIAO_137 §4, **KSI-CMT (continuous monitoring)**, KSI-RPL, and
   KSI-SCR currently have **no local KSI rules**. VDR/VER evidence is
   primarily KSI-CMT-shaped, so the existing coverage gap directly
   limits how much VDR/VER evidence the substrate can emit natively
   today.

### What this does NOT change

- **UIAO core / non-federal verticals.** BOD 26-04 and VDR/VER are a
  federal-vertical concern; the vertical-agnostic substrate engine is
  unaffected (per ADR-085 positioning).
- **The BOD 25-01 drift-ledger answer (UIAO_132 §4).** BOD 26-04
  supersedes BOD 22-01 / 19-02, **not** BOD 25-01 (logging). The SCuBA
  drift-ledger continuity story is independent and unchanged.
- **The OSCAL/KSI emission pipeline.** VDR/VER evidence rides the
  existing emission surface (UIAO_133); no parallel pipeline is needed,
  consistent with ADR-047 D1.

## 4. Proposed remedy

### Internal remedy (inside UIAO scope)

1. **Fire the UIAO_132 §2.4 migration gate and add a VER section.**
   Record the 2026-12-07 mandate and BOD 26-04 hook against the
   Pathway-1 gate, and add a VER / VER-EVA-EIR subsection that binds
   internet-reachability evaluation to the existing exposure primitive
   in `src/uiao/modernization/locpath/entra_exposure.py`. *(Landed with
   this finding — UIAO_132 v0.3.)*

2. **Re-model the vulnerability SLA against BOD 26-04 (successor ADR to
   ADR-043 D2).** Replace the flat 72-hour critical clock with a
   four-variable (exposure / KEV / automatability / impact) tiered
   ladder. Doctrinal — lands as its own ADR with governance review, not
   in this finding's PR.

3. **Advance the CR26 snapshot pin (ADR-061 D2) once VDR/VER finalize,
   then close the UIAO_137 FRR-group mapping.** Sequenced after FedRAMP
   publishes the finalized CR26; the pin-advance PR carries the VDR/VER
   rules and the FRR mapping that UIAO_137 currently defers.

4. **Seed KSI-CMT local rules.** Begin closing the KSI-CMT (and, as
   VDR/VER scope clarifies, KSI-RPL) coverage gap named in UIAO_137 §4
   so VDR/VER evidence can be emitted natively. Each rule lands with
   happy-path + failure-mode tests per the AGENTS.md operating rule.

Items 2–4 are tracked here so they are not lost; only item 1 lands in
this finding's PR, keeping it reviewable.

### External remedy (outside UIAO scope)

1. **FedRAMP finalizes VDR and VER within CR26** (promised end of June
   2026). The substrate cannot pin rules that have not published; item 3
   above is gated on this.
2. **The hosting CSP adopts VDR/VER for its government cloud offering**
   by the 2026-12-07 mandate, so inherited vulnerability-management
   evidence becomes available to tenants (same inheritance pattern as
   [FINDING-002](./fedramp-20x-moderate-pilot.qmd)).
3. **CISA / FedRAMP companion guidance on the four-variable matrix.**
   Until "automatable" and "internet-reachable" have stable operational
   definitions, 3PAOs will score identical findings differently —
   mirroring the RFC-0005 "likely impact" interpretation risk in
   FINDING-002.

The external remedy is not a prerequisite for UIAO to deliver value;
the in-scope internal items proceed on the substrate's own clock.
